content:
kevin: quick sync: after the last churn I'm worried our eviction+failover loop is amplifying short spikes. sketch: introduce per-tenant eviction budget + consent-stamp to prevent cross-border movements during budget windows.

anya: eviction budget? curious how you define it and where it's tracked.

kevin: think of it like a token bucket: tenant has X eviction tokens; each region swap consumes a token; tokens refill slowly. if tokens exhausted, swaps that would violate residency require operator confirm or are blocked. prevents thrash.

rav: sounds promising. we should also record a consent-stamp on each tenant record: hard-residency|consented-date|consent-source. swaps that would cross a hard-residency barrier are aborted unless operator-ack. soft-consent can be overridden by budget but flagged.

anya: how do we handle emergency outages? we can't let a token bucket block disaster response. need an override path: emergency_failover that logs and increments an operator audit counter.

kevin: agreed. emergency_failover bypasses budget but sets tenant into "post-emergency_cooldown" with increased refill time and emits a high-severity alert. also requires a human review within 24h.

prio-bot: reminder: new config feature schedule: eviction-budget v0.1 -> canary 2025-10-14T01:00Z.

rav: implementation note: where to store budget state? control plane DB primary with lightweight cache in proxies for fast checks. proxies must treat cache as advisory and validate with control plane if budget low/zero.

anya: also need metrics: token_count, last_swap_ts, blocked_by_budget counter, emergency_overrides. dashboards + SLI alert if blocked_by_budget spikes unexpectedly.

sec: privacy note: consent-stamp must include source (user, legal, admin) and be tamper-evident. sign the stamp with control-plane key and surface it to proxies as x-consent-stamp header. encrypt in private deployments.

kevin: tie-ins: prewarm system should respect budget+consent: prewarm across borders consumes a token unless the tenant has soft-consent. prewarm failures should not auto-consume tokens.

rav: and testing: 1) simulate p95 blips to see if budget reduces swap rate, 2) simulate outage that requires emergency_failover and verify audit flow, 3) load test token refill under scale.

anya: UX: add operator dashboard to view per-tenant budget and manual add/remove tokens, plus a bulk-reclaim utility (for tenants who migrate permanently).

kevin: next steps I'll draft RFC section with config defaults (tokens=3, refill_rate=1 per 6h, emergency_override=true) and runbook for emergency flow. any objections?

rav: none. will take proxy cache sketch.

sec: will draft consent-stamp signing spec.

kevin: thanks all. opening RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:
